    Strong leadership isn’t just about delivering today, it’s about building the capability we need for the future. That’s why developing our leaders continues to be a real priority for Airways. Our People Experience Manager Lisa Boltman, and Manager of Air Traffic Services Development Jennifer Nepton recently shared their experience in the University of Auckland’s Transitioning to C-Suite programme. What’s important is how that learning is coming back into our business. Over the past few years, insights from the programme have helped shape our leadership and performance frameworks and influenced how we approach strategy and organisational development.     Airways New Zealand and Airservices Australia have been recognised on the global stage with a category win at the Seamless Skies awards at Airspace World 2026. We’re honoured to have won the Collaborative Operations for Sustainable Skies category of the Seamless Skies Awards, for our joint approach in partnership with Airservices Australia to build a more resilient and efficient aviation system across one of the world’s most geographically dispersed regions.  Airways Chief Executive James Young, and Airservices Australia Chief Technology Officer Mark Hind accepted the award during a ceremony at Airspace World in Lisbon. Together, we're co-designing and delivering initiatives that strengthen air traffic control capability and improve system performance. This includes shared training pathways, mobile and remote simulation and ATC trainee selection through Airways International Ltd (AIL), and the development of contingency capability to support each other’s airspace during disruptions.     We’re very pleased that our collaboration with Airservices Australia has been shortlisted for a CANSO Seamless Skies Award this year.   In December we signed an MOU with Airservices Australia to strengthen collaboration on initiatives that enhance the safety, efficiency and resilience of air traffic services across the region. One of the first initiatives underway is supporting Airservices Australia to train new and existing air traffic controllers through our commercial division, Airways International Ltd (AIL).   We are up against some strong competition, and we look forward to hearing the winners announced at Airspace World next month.    Congratulations to everyone involved, and thank you to CANSO for recognising innovation and collaboration across global airspace management.     We’re marking Pride Month by strengthening our partnership with Pride Pledge 🏳️🌈 and reaffirming our commitment to inclusion and belonging. As we head into Pride Month in Ōtautahi (Christchurch), home to our largest campus, it’s a meaningful time to reflect on the role we all play in creating a workplace where everyone feels safe, respected and able to thrive. In 2023, we achieved our first Rainbow Tick accreditation, an important milestone in building a workplace where people feel valued and supported. Partnering with Pride Pledge builds on that foundation, connecting us with initiatives across Aotearoa and supporting the ongoing work of our Rainbow Employee Network and allies across Airways. Last month, we recognised Pride Month in Tāmaki Makaurau (Auckland) with our Rainbow Employee Network hosting a Putt with Pride event. Inclusion is an ongoing effort and we’re proud to keep listening, learning and leading.

    This Sunday we mark International Women’s Day. For Airways, it’s a chance to celebrate the women helping to shape the future of aviation. While aviation has traditionally had fewer women in operational and technical roles, that is changing. Across the industry, there is a growing focus on encouraging more women to explore aviation careers and ensuring the sector reflects the communities we serve. At Airways, this work is part of our commitment to strengthening the aviation workforce and supporting more women into technical roles, aligning with the goals of the New Zealand Aviation Action Plan. Ahead of Sunday, we’re sharing the story of one of our many talented technical specialists. Hear Andria talk about her pathway into aviation and what she enjoys about working in such a critical role.

    An outstanding effort delivered some impressive results in the Aotearoa Bike Challenge. Airways riders clocked up 11,911km through February and smashed our 10,000km goal. Even better, 4,599km replaced vehicle trips, helping save 833kg of CO₂e in just one month. Our people's efforts are a great demonstration of the impact active transport can have for wellbeing and sustainability.
